title: DFTB coupled with NEGF study of the structural, electronic and transport properties of goldene 2D material
abstract: We report the structural, electronic, and transport properties of the goldene 2D material using the density functional tight-binding (DFTB) method. Electronic transport calculations were conducted in conjunction with the non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) technique. Our study reveals that the Au 2D material is dynamically and thermally stable, and it possesses good elastic properties. On the other hand, goldene has a linear relationship between current and voltage at low potentials, indicating its metallic character. The calculated current-potential curve correlates well with transmission functions and the electronic density of states around the Fermi level. We also investigated the electronic structure and magnetic properties of silicon (Si)-doped Au 2D material. Our results show that the Si atom can induce a local magnetic state in the goldene monolayer. The resulting magnetic moment is 0.63 $μ_B$.
summary: This theoretical study characterizes the physical properties of goldene 2D material using advanced computational techniques like DFTB+NEGF. It confirms the material's mechanical robustness and metallic conductivity while demonstrating that doping with Silicon can induce a measurable local magnetic moment, making it interesting for spintronic applications.
main_problem: To investigate the structural, electronic, and transport properties of goldene (Au) 2D material, including how substitutional doping with Silicon (Si) affects its magnetic behavior.
main_result: Goldene is found to be dynamically and thermally stable, exhibiting metallic conductivity. Si doping successfully induces a local magnetic moment ($\approx 0.63 \mu_B$) in the otherwise nonmagnetic monolayer.
method: The study employs Density Functional Tight-Binding (DFTB) coupled with Non-Equilibrium Green's Functions (NEGF) for transport calculations, supplemented by Molecular Dynamics (MD) and phonon dispersion analysis for stability assessment.
model_or_system: The primary system is the planar goldene 2D material. The model is extended to include substitutional Si doping at an Au vacancy site within a supercell geometry, analyzed as a two-probe electronic device.
key_observables: Current-potential ($I$-$V$) curve, zero-bias transmission function $T(E)$, magnetic moment ($\mu$), elastic constants ($C_{ij}$), and lattice thermal conductivity.
important_parameters: Temperature up to 700 K; applied bias voltage (non-equilibrium); doping concentration/site.
main_assumptions: The accuracy of the results relies on the DFTB approximation, and transport calculations utilize the Landauer formula formalism within the NEGF framework.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phonon dispersion curves confirming dynamic stability, MD energy vs. time plots showing thermal stability up to 700 K, electronic band structures confirming metallic nature, and spin density maps visualizing the induced magnetic moment upon Si doping.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression from structural/mechanical characterization (stability, elastic constants) to electronic structure analysis (band theory), culminating in non-equilibrium transport calculations ($I$-$V$ curves) and finally investigating defect chemistry and magnetism via Si doping.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information directly, the use of NEGF/DFTB methods for calculating quantized conductance and spin transport in low-dimensional systems is foundational to understanding nanoscale electronic devices relevant to future quantum technologies.
